title: NDIS Support Coordinator Salary: Hourly to Annual Guide
description: Calculate your NDIS support coordinator salary from hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay. Includes award rates, tax, super, and casual loading under the SCHADS Award.
salarySummary: For a full-time NDIS support coordinator working 38 hours per week, the annual salary is the hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks per year, with superannuation paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the typical hourly rate for an NDIS support coordinator under the SCHADS Award?
faqs.a: The Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award (SCHADS Award) sets minimum rates for NDIS support coordinators classified as social and community services employees. From 1 July 2026, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, but award rates are higher. For example, Level 2 pay point 4 (a common classification for experienced support coordinators) was $995.60 per week in 2017 rates; current rates are updated annually. Actual pay depends on your specific pay point and experience. Use the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page for guidance.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours per week (usually 38 for full-time) and then multiply by 52 weeks. For example, $35 per hour × 38 hours × 52 = $69,160 gross. If you are casual, add 25% loading before entering the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) before using the timesheet. The timesheet assumes a base rate without loading. Use the [the timesheet](/) for a base rate.

faqs.q: Do I need to include casual loading when using the timesheet?
faqs.a: Yes. The timesheet has a checkbox for casual loading. If you are a casual employee, your base rate is the base rate plus 25% loading. Do not enter the loading into the rate. The checkbox adds it on top. For award employees, the loading is already included in the rate. See the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) for details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the NDIS Support Coordinator Salary

NDIS support coordinators are covered by the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award (SCHADS Award). This award sets minimum wages for social and community services employees, including those working in disability services. The national minimum wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for 38 hours per week, but award rates are higher for most support coordinators. For example, a Level 2 pay point 4 employee under the award (as shown in the Fair Work Ombudsman pay guide ) would have a weekly rate that translates to an hourly rate above the minimum. Actual pay depends on your classification, experience, and whether you are full-time, part-time, or casual.

### How to Convert Hourly to Annual

To estimate your annual salary, use the formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For a full-time NDIS support coordinator working 38 hours per week, this gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. For example, if your hourly rate is $35.00:

- Weekly: $35.00 × 38 = $1,330.00
- Fortnightly: $1,330.00 × 2 = $2,660.00
- Annual: $1,330.00 × 52 = $69,160.00

If you are part-time, use your actual weekly hours. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and choose to add casual loading if applicable.

### Award Coverage and Minimum Rates

The SCHADS Award requires a minimum of 38 hours per week for full-time employees. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. The minimum engagement for social and community services employees (including disability support workers) is 3 hours per shift. For all other employees, it is 2 hours. Salary packaging is allowed under the award.

### Tax and Superannuation

Your annual gross salary is subject to Australian resident tax for 2026–27: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a $69,160 annual salary, super would be approximately $8,299.20 per year.

### Using the Timesheet

The [the timesheet](/) on this site calculates your annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay from your hourly rate. It assumes 38 hours per week for full-time. If you are casual, check the box to add 25% loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading. The calculator then estimates tax and super based on the on-site reference figures.

### Important Notes

This estimate assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
